# Unified Notation and Conventions {.unnumbered}

This note is the canonical notation registry for the project. Chapters may introduce local symbols, but they must not redefine symbols listed here. When a textbook uses different notation, translate it into these conventions.

## Core conventions {.unnumbered .unlisted}

1. Scalars use italic lowercase letters, vectors use bold lowercase letters, and matrices use bold uppercase letters.
2. Vectors are column vectors unless stated otherwise.
3. SI units are used in calculations. Angles are expressed in radians.
4. Coordinate frames are right-handed. A leading left superscript identifies the frame in which coordinates are expressed.
5. Continuous time uses $t$; sampled time uses the integer index $k$.
6. A wide hat over a twist, as in $\widehat{\boldsymbol\xi}$, denotes the declared Lie-algebra hat operator and is not an estimate.
7. Bold symbols and scalar symbols with the same letter are distinct; for example, $\mathbf R$ is a rotation matrix whereas $R$ may be a signed turning radius.
8. A symbol may have a different local meaning only in a clearly separated mathematical domain where its type and meaning are explicitly redeclared; for example, $m$ may denote a matrix dimension in a generic linear-algebra statement and robot mass in a dynamics model.

## Part I: Motion, Mechanics, and Control {.unnumbered .unlisted}

### Notation introduced in @sec-linear-algebra-foundations {.unnumbered .unlisted}

| Symbol | Meaning | Units or convention |
|---|---|---|
| $a,\alpha$ | Scalar quantity | Depends on the quantity |
| $m,n,i,j$ | Integer dimensions or indices | Declared locally |
| $\mathbb R$ | Set of real numbers | — |
| $\mathbb R^n,\mathbb R^{m\times n}$ | Real coordinate columns and real matrices | Dimensions shown by the superscripts |
| $\mathbb R_{\geq0},\mathbb R_{>0}$ | Nonnegative and strictly positive real numbers | — |
| $\mathbf{v}\in\mathbb{R}^n$ | Column vector with $n$ components | Depends on the quantity |
| $\mathbf{A}\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$ | Matrix with $m$ rows and $n$ columns | Depends on the map |
| $\mathbf{I}_n$ | $n\times n$ identity matrix | Dimensionless |
| $\mathbf{0}_n$ | Zero vector with $n$ components | Depends on the quantity |
| $(\cdot)^\mathsf{T}$ | Transpose | — |
| $(\cdot)^{-1}$ | Inverse, when it exists | — |
| $\lVert\mathbf{v}\rVert_2$ | Euclidean norm of $\mathbf{v}$ | Same units as $\mathbf{v}$ |
| $\det(\mathbf A)$ | Determinant of a square matrix | Depends on the matrix units |
| $\operatorname{rank}(\mathbf A)$ | Dimension of the column space of $\mathbf A$ | Nonnegative integer |
| $\operatorname{nullity}(\mathbf A)$ | Dimension of the null space of $\mathbf A$ | Nonnegative integer |
| $\operatorname{span}(\mathbf v_1,\ldots,\mathbf v_k)$ | Set of all linear combinations of the listed vectors | Same vector space as the vectors |
| $\operatorname{Col}(\mathbf A),\mathcal N(\mathbf A)$ | Column space and null space of $\mathbf A$ | Subspaces of the output and input spaces |
| $O(n),SO(n)$ | Orthogonal group and special orthogonal group of real $n\times n$ matrices | $\mathbf Q^\mathsf T\mathbf Q=\mathbf I_n$; $SO(n)$ additionally requires $\det\mathbf Q=1$ |

### Notation introduced in @sec-geometry-coordinate-frames {.unnumbered .unlisted}

| Symbol | Meaning | Units or convention |
|---|---|---|
| $\{a\}$ | Coordinate frame named $a$ | Right-handed |
| $O_a$ | Origin of frame $\{a\}$ | — |
| $\mathbf{e}_{x,a},\mathbf{e}_{y,a},\mathbf{e}_{z,a}$ | Unit basis vectors of frame $\{a\}$ | Dimensionless |
| ${}^{a}\mathbf{v}$ | Coordinates of geometric vector $\mathbf{v}$ expressed in frame $\{a\}$ | Depends on $\mathbf{v}$ |
| ${}^{a}\mathbf{p}_P$ | Position of point $P$ relative to $O_a$, expressed in frame $\{a\}$ | $\mathrm{m}$ |
| ${}^{a}\mathbf r_{OP}$ | Relative-position vector from point $O$ to point $P$, expressed in frame $\{a\}$ | $\mathrm{m}$ |
| $\mathbf{R}_{ab}$ | Rotation mapping coordinates from frame $\{b\}$ to frame $\{a\}$ | $\mathbf{R}_{ab}\in SO(2)$ or $SO(3)$ |
| ${}^{a}\mathbf{p}_b$ | Position of origin $O_b$ relative to $O_a$, expressed in frame $\{a\}$ | $\mathrm{m}$ |
| $\mathbf u\times\mathbf v$ | Three-dimensional cross product of vectors expressed in the same right-handed orthonormal frame | Product of the input units |
| $\boldsymbol\omega$ | Three-dimensional angular-velocity vector | $\mathrm{rad\,s^{-1}}$ |

### Notation introduced in @sec-differential-drive-model {.unnumbered .unlisted}

| Symbol                                 | Meaning                                                                | Units or convention                                     |
| -------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| $t$                                    | Continuous time                                                        | $\mathrm{s}$                                           |
| $k\in\mathbb N_0$                    | Sample index, where $\mathbb N_0=\{0,1,2,\ldots\}$                  | Dimensionless integer                                   |
| $t_k$                                  | Time at sample $k$                                                     | $\mathrm{s}$                                           |
| $\Delta t=t_{k+1}-t_k$                | Sampling or numerical-integration interval                            | $\mathrm{s}$                                           |
| $\dot{\mathbf{x}},\ddot{\mathbf{x}}$ | First and second derivatives with respect to time                    | Quantity per $\mathrm{s}$ and per $\mathrm{s}^2$      |
| $\{w\},\{b\}$                          | World and robot body frames                                            | —                                                       |
| $O_w,O_b$                              | Origins of the world and body frames                                   | —                                                       |
| $\mathbf{q}=[x\;y\;\theta]^\mathsf{T}$ | Planar robot pose coordinates in the world frame                       | $\mathrm{m},\mathrm{m},\mathrm{rad}$                    |
| $\theta$                               | Counter-clockwise heading of $\{b\}$ relative to $\{w\}$               | $\mathrm{rad}$                                          |
| $\mathbf u=[v\;\omega]^\mathsf T$      | Planar body-velocity input                                             | $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}},\mathrm{rad\,s^{-1}}$               |
| $v,\omega$                             | Signed body-forward speed and counter-clockwise yaw rate               | $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}},\mathrm{rad\,s^{-1}}$               |
| $\phi_L,\phi_R$                        | Left and right wheel angles                                            | $\mathrm{rad}$                                          |
| $\dot{\phi}_L,\dot{\phi}_R$            | Left and right wheel angular speeds                                    | $\mathrm{rad\,s^{-1}}$                                  |
| $v_L,v_R$                              | Signed longitudinal ground speeds of the left and right wheels         | $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$                                    |
| $r,L$                                  | Effective wheel radius and track width between wheel contact lines     | $\mathrm{m}$                                            |
| $C$                                    | Instantaneous centre of curvature for planar motion                    | Geometric point                                         |
| $\rho$                                 | Nonnegative radial distance declared in the local geometric context    | $\mathrm{m}$                                            |
| $R$                                    | Signed turning radius; positive for an ICC on the robot's left         | $\mathrm{m}$; distinct from rotation matrix $\mathbf R$ |
| $\Delta\ell,\Delta\theta$              | Signed arc-length and heading changes over an interval                 | $\mathrm{m},\mathrm{rad}$                               |
| $\mathbf q_k^{\mathrm E}$              | Forward Euler approximation of the pose at sample $k$                  | $\mathrm{m},\mathrm{m},\mathrm{rad}$                    |
| $E(\Delta t)$                          | Declared numerical-integration error magnitude at step size $\Delta t$ | Depends on the error definition                         |
| $e_p$                                  | One-step position-error magnitude in the declared integration comparison | $\mathrm m$                                          |
| $O(h^p)$                               | Quantity bounded in magnitude by a constant times $h^p$ as $h\to0$   | Units follow the bounded quantity                       |
| $\operatorname{sinc}(z)$              | Unnormalised sinc function, $\sin z/z$ for $z\neq0$ and $1$ for $z=0$ | Dimensionless argument and value                      |

### Notation introduced in @sec-planar-rigid-body-motion {.unnumbered .unlisted}

| Symbol | Meaning | Units or convention |
|---|---|---|
| ${}^{a}\overline{\mathbf p}_P$ | Homogeneous point coordinate obtained by appending $1$ to ${}^{a}\mathbf p_P$ | Position entries in $\mathrm m$; final entry dimensionless |
| $SO(2)$ | Special orthogonal group of planar rotation matrices | $\mathbf R^\mathsf T\mathbf R=\mathbf I_2$, $\det\mathbf R=1$ |
| $SE(2)$ | Special Euclidean group of planar rigid transformations | Planar rotation and translation represented together |
| $\mathbf{T}_{ab}$ | Homogeneous transform mapping coordinates from frame $\{b\}$ to frame $\{a\}$ | $\mathbf{T}_{ab}\in SE(2)$ |
| $T_{\mathbf I_2}SO(2)$ | Tangent space of $SO(2)$ at the identity rotation $\mathbf I_2$ | Linear space of rotation-curve derivatives through $\mathbf I_2$ |
| $T_{\mathbf I_3}SE(2)$ | Tangent space of $SE(2)$ at the identity transformation $\mathbf I_3$ | Linear space of transformation-curve derivatives through $\mathbf I_3$ |
| $\mathbf S_2$ | Planar skew generator $\begin{bmatrix}0&-1\\1&0\end{bmatrix}$ | Dimensionless |
| $\mathfrak{so}(2)$ | Lie algebra and identity tangent space of $SO(2)$ | $2\times2$ real skew-symmetric matrices |
| $\mathfrak{se}(2)$ | Lie algebra and identity tangent space of $SE(2)$ | Structured $3\times3$ infinitesimal planar rigid-motion matrices |
| $\boldsymbol\xi=[\boldsymbol\nu^\mathsf T\;\omega]^\mathsf T$ | Planar twist coordinate column with linear part $\boldsymbol\nu\in\mathbb R^2$ and angular part $\omega\in\mathbb R$ | $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ and $\mathrm{rad\,s^{-1}}$ |
| $\widehat{\boldsymbol\xi}$ | Hat-operator matrix representing $\boldsymbol\xi$ in $\mathfrak{se}(2)$ | Upper-left block in $\mathrm{s^{-1}}$; translation column in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ |
| $(\cdot)^\vee$ | Vee operator, inverse of the declared hat operator | Returns the twist coordinate column |
| $\boldsymbol\xi_b,\boldsymbol\xi_w$ | Body and spatial twist coordinates for the same instantaneous motion | Body axes/body origin and world axes/world origin conventions |
| $\boldsymbol\nu_b,\boldsymbol\nu_w$ | Linear parts of the body and spatial twists | $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ |
| $\operatorname{Ad}_{\mathbf T}$ | Adjoint mapping that changes twist coordinates according to rigid transform $\mathbf T$ | Matrix dimensions and mixed units follow the twist convention |
| $\ell$ | Declared characteristic length used to compare linear and angular twist components | $\mathrm m$ |

### Notation introduced in @sec-spatial-rigid-body-motion {.unnumbered .unlisted}

| Symbol | Meaning | Units or convention |
|---|---|---|
| $\mathcal C$ | Configuration space: the set of all configurations allowed by the model | May be curved and need not be a vector space |
| $\mathbf q\in\mathcal C$ | Configuration or a chosen column of generalised coordinates | Components and units depend on the system |
| $n_{\mathrm{dof}}$ | Number of configuration degrees of freedom | Nonnegative integer |
| $n_v,n_c$ | Numbers of scalar variables and independent regular equality constraints in a local count | Nonnegative integers |
| $\mathcal M$ | Smooth manifold: a space that locally resembles a Euclidean coordinate space | Dimension declared locally |
| $T_{\mathbf G}\mathcal M$ | Tangent space of manifold $\mathcal M$ at $\mathbf G$ | Linear space of curve derivatives through $\mathbf G$ |
| $SO(3)$ | Special orthogonal group of spatial rotation matrices | $\mathbf R^\mathsf T\mathbf R=\mathbf I_3$, $\det\mathbf R=1$ |
| $SE(3)$ | Special Euclidean group of spatial rigid transformations | Spatial rotation and translation represented together |
| $[\mathbf{v}]_\times$ | Skew-symmetric matrix satisfying $[\mathbf{v}]_\times\mathbf{w}=\mathbf{v}\times\mathbf{w}$ | Same units as $\mathbf{v}$ |

### Notation introduced in @sec-dynamics-actuator-limits {.unnumbered .unlisted}

| Symbol | Meaning | Units or convention |
|---|---|---|
| $s(t),v(t),a(t)$ | Signed one-dimensional position, velocity, and acceleration | $\mathrm m,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}},\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$ |
| $m$ | Robot mass | $\mathrm{kg}$ |
| $\mathbf F,F$ | Force vector and force magnitude | $\mathrm N$ |
| $F_j,F_{\mathrm{net}}$ | Signed component of external force $j$ and their signed net sum | $\mathrm N$ |
| $F_{\mathrm{drive}},F_{\mathrm{resist}}$ | Nonnegative drive and resistance force magnitudes in the declared direction | $\mathrm N$ |
| $\boldsymbol\rho$ | Position vector from a chosen moment point to a force application point | $\mathrm m$ |
| $\boldsymbol\tau_O,\tau$ | Torque vector about point $O$ and its magnitude | $\mathrm{N\,m}$ |
| $\tau_i,F_i$ | Signed axle torque and longitudinal ground force for wheel $i\in\{L,R\}$ | $\mathrm{N\,m},\mathrm N$ |
| $I_i$ | Wheel mass moment of inertia about its axle | $\mathrm{kg\,m^2}$ |
| $\ddot\phi_i$ | Wheel angular acceleration | $\mathrm{rad\,s^{-2}}$ |
| $G$ | Positive gearbox reduction ratio | Dimensionless |
| $\eta$ | Gearbox efficiency for the declared power-flow direction | Dimensionless, $0<\eta\leq1$ |
| $\dot\phi_m,\dot\phi_w$ | Motor-shaft and wheel-side angular speeds | $\mathrm{rad\,s^{-1}}$ |
| $\tau_m,\tau_w$ | Motor-shaft and wheel-side torques | $\mathrm{N\,m}$ |
| $P=\tau\dot\phi$ | Rotational mechanical power | $\mathrm W=\mathrm{N\,m\,s^{-1}}$ |
